questions.text: In 'Getting Started', who did not complete his part of the project on time?
questions.explanation: Everyone except Azlan completed their work on time.

questions.text: How did Ayesha respond to Azlan's behaviour?
options: She was patient and shared a book with him
questions.explanation: Ayesha was patient with Azlan and shared a book to help him finish.

questions.text: Who is the writer's role model in the lesson 'Patience'?
questions.explanation: The writer's role model is Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), complete in all aspects.

questions.text: Rasoolullah (PBUH) was called Saadiq and Al-Amin because of his:
questions.explanation: He was called Saadiq and Al-Amin for his honest, truthful nature.

questions.text: Which city did Rasoolullah (PBUH) travel to, to spread the message of Islam, where people pelted him with stones?
questions.explanation: In Taif a mob pelted him with pebbles, yet he prayed for them.

questions.text: Who accompanied Rasoolullah (PBUH) on the journey to Taif?
questions.explanation: He was accompanied by Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha.

questions.text: How did Rasoolullah (PBUH) respond to the people of Taif?
options: He prayed for them to be guided
questions.explanation: Despite being hurt, he prayed that they or their children would accept the right path.

questions.text: The main moral value taught in Unit 1 is:
questions.explanation: The unit 'Patience' shows the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as an example of patience for all mankind.

questions.text: Letters that are spelt in a word but not pronounced are called:
questions.explanation: Silent letters are written but not pronounced, e.g. k in knife, w in write.

questions.text: In the word 'knife', which letter is silent?
questions.explanation: In 'knife' the k is silent.

questions.text: What is the name of the poem in Unit 2 (Be Grateful)?
questions.explanation: The dialogue refers to the poem 'Allah Loves Me'.

questions.text: Where does the poet see Allah in the first line?
questions.explanation: The poem begins: 'I see You in the stars'.

questions.text: What does the poet ask Allah in the last line?
questions.explanation: The poem ends 'O Allah! Just love me more!'

questions.text: According to Maryam, what message does the poem give?
options: Allah loves us and is always there for us
questions.explanation: Maryam says the poem tells us Allah loves us and is always with us in sadness and happiness.

questions.text: Which article is used before 'umbrella'?
questions.explanation: Words starting with a vowel sound take 'an': an umbrella.

questions.text: Which article is correct: 'He was ___ famous umpire'?
questions.explanation: 'Famous' begins with a consonant sound, so we use 'a'.

questions.text: Which expression is used to give an opinion?
questions.explanation: Expressions like 'In my opinion' and 'I think' are used to share opinions.

questions.text: Fatima Jinnah was the younger sister of:
questions.explanation: Miss Fatima Jinnah was the younger sister of Quaid-e-Azam.

questions.text: What was Fatima Jinnah's profession before she joined the Pakistan Movement?
questions.explanation: She was a dentist by profession and later gave it up to help her brother.

questions.text: Which title was given to Fatima Jinnah?
questions.explanation: Due to her untiring efforts she got the title 'Maadar-e-Millat'.

questions.text: Fatima Jinnah formed the Women's Relief Committee, which was later renamed:
questions.explanation: The Women's Relief Committee was later renamed 'All Pakistan Women's Association'.

questions.text: Dr. Ruth Pfau devoted her life to fighting which disease in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Dr. Ruth Pfau, a German doctor and nun, fought leprosy in Pakistan.

questions.text: Dr. Ruth Pfau is known as:
questions.explanation: She is known as the Mother Teresa of Pakistan.

questions.text: How many leprosy clinics did Dr. Ruth Pfau set up across Pakistan?
questions.explanation: She set up 150 leprosy clinics across the country.

questions.text: Arfa Karim became the world's youngest:
questions.explanation: At nine she became the world's youngest Microsoft Certified Professional.

questions.text: Samina Baig was the first Pakistani woman to climb:
questions.explanation: Samina Khayal Baig is the first Pakistani woman to climb Mount Everest.

questions.text: Samina Baig belongs to Shimshal village in:
questions.explanation: She belongs to Shimshal village in Hunza, Gojal, Gilgit-Baltistan.

questions.text: Where did the writer's grandparents live?
questions.explanation: The writer visited grandparents in Swat during the summer vacation.

questions.text: Why was the writer shocked on reaching the farmhouse?
options: The grass was burnt and the trees had wilted
questions.explanation: There was burnt yellow grass with bushes and the tall trees had wilted.

questions.text: Why had the farmhouse become neglected?
questions.explanation: The gardener who took care of it had passed away due to illness.

questions.text: How long did it take the children to restore the farmhouse?
questions.explanation: They got everything back the way it used to be within a month.

questions.text: What exciting activity did the children do in Swat Valley?
questions.explanation: They rode zip lines from one hill to another.

questions.text: According to 'Getting Started', trees reduce air pollution by using:
questions.explanation: Trees use carbon dioxide and provide humans with oxygen.

questions.text: In the poem 'Amazing Planet', who is speaking?
questions.explanation: The Earth speaks: 'I am your home, but you destroy my skin and bone.'

questions.text: What does the Earth ask for in the poem?
options: No more plastic and no more waste
questions.explanation: The Earth says, 'No more plastic, and no more waste.'

questions.text: The main theme of 'Amazing Planet' is:
questions.explanation: The poem asks us to stop polluting the Earth, our only home.

questions.text: When the weather stays the same for a certain period in an area, it becomes a:
questions.explanation: Getting Started explains that weather staying for a certain period becomes a season; seasons make up the climate.

questions.text: Which word begins with a three-consonant cluster?
questions.explanation: 'Straw' begins with s-t-r, a three-consonant cluster.

questions.text: Which sentence politely makes a request?
options: Could I borrow your camera for this trip?
questions.explanation: 'Could I borrow...?' is a polite way to make a request.

questions.text: Why did Dr. Haroon visit the school?
options: To talk about personal hygiene and COVID-19
questions.explanation: He came to talk about personal hygiene and raise awareness about COVID-19.

questions.text: For at least how long should we wash our hands?
questions.explanation: Aqsa said we should wash our hands for at least 20 seconds.

questions.text: What should we do while sneezing?
questions.explanation: Wasif said we should cover our face while sneezing.

questions.text: What should we do before taking any medicine?
questions.explanation: Dr. Haroon said tell your elders first; never take medicine unless elders give it.

questions.text: Which helps to stop the spread of viral diseases, according to Dr. Haroon?
options: Wearing a mask and physical distancing
questions.explanation: He said never forget to wear a mask and keep physical distance.

questions.text: Which of these keeps us strong and fit?
questions.explanation: Dr. Haroon said eating healthy food and drinking clean water keeps us strong and fit.

questions.text: In 'What Goes Around, Comes Around', where did the frog invite the mouse?
questions.explanation: The frog invited the mouse to come and see the wonderful underwater world.

questions.text: Why did the mouse hesitate to go with the frog?
questions.explanation: The mouse said, 'I would love to go with you but I cannot swim.'

questions.text: How did the frog tie the mouse to himself?
options: With a rope around the waist
By tying the mouse's foot to his own with a thread
questions.explanation: The frog tied the mouse's foot to his own with a piece of thread.

questions.text: What happened to the mouse in the pond?
questions.explanation: The poor mouse drowned while the unkind frog swam about.

questions.text: Which bird pounced on the floating mouse?
questions.explanation: A hawk saw the mouse and pounced upon it, dragging the frog too.

questions.text: What is the moral of the fable?
options: Slow and steady wins the race
As you sow, so shall you reap
questions.explanation: The moral: As you sow, so shall you reap.

questions.text: A short story with animal characters that teaches a moral is called a:
questions.explanation: A fable is a short story, often with animal characters, that teaches a lesson.

questions.text: What did Raffay find on the road?
questions.explanation: After Mohsin passed by on a bicycle, Raffay saw a wallet lying on the road.

questions.text: How much money was in the wallet?
questions.explanation: He found three thousand rupees in the wallet.

questions.text: Whose wallet was it?
questions.explanation: The wallet belonged to his classmate Mohsin.

questions.text: Which two things that his teacher said made Raffay feel sorry?
options: Never tell a lie, and return things found unattended
questions.explanation: The teacher had said: never tell a lie, and return unattended things to their owner.

questions.text: What did Raffay finally do with the wallet?
questions.explanation: Raffay went to Mohsin's house, told the whole story and handed over the wallet.

questions.text: What did Mohsin praise Raffay for?
questions.explanation: Mohsin thanked Allah and praised Raffay for his honesty.

questions.text: What is the title of the poem in the unit 'Patriotism'?
questions.explanation: The poem in Unit 9 is 'A Nation's Strength'.

questions.text: According to the poem, what makes a people great and strong?
options: Men (people) who stand for truth and honour
questions.explanation: 'Not gold but only men can make a people great and strong.'

questions.text: Brave men in the poem work while others:
questions.explanation: 'Brave men who work, while others sleep, who dare while others fly.'

questions.text: Why do we celebrate Pakistan Day?
options: To remember the Lahore Resolution of 1940
questions.explanation: Pakistan Day remembers the Lahore Resolution of 1940, which proposed a separate Muslim state.

questions.text: The Lahore Resolution is also called the:
questions.explanation: It proposed an independent Muslim state, so it is also called the Pakistan Resolution.

questions.text: According to 'Getting Started', what makes a nation strong?
questions.explanation: Education makes a nation strong by making people learned and skilful.

questions.text: In 'laughed', the -ed ending is pronounced as:
questions.explanation: After k, s, ch, sh, f, p sounds the -ed is pronounced /t/: laughed, asked.

questions.text: What did Suleman want to buy for Eid-ul-Azha?
questions.explanation: Suleman wanted to buy a goat for Eid.

questions.text: On which date is Eid-ul-Azha celebrated?
questions.explanation: Father said Eid-ul-Azha is celebrated on the 10th of Zil-Hajj every year.

questions.text: Eid-ul-Azha reminds us of the great sacrifice of:
questions.explanation: Muslims sacrifice animals to remember the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim and his son Hazrat Ismail.

questions.text: What do we do with the meat of the sacrificed animal?
options: Share it among friends, relatives and the poor
questions.explanation: We share the meat among friends, relatives and the needy.

questions.text: When did Suleman and his father go to the cattle market?
questions.explanation: Father said they would go to the cattle market on Sunday.

questions.text: What colour was the goat they bought?
questions.explanation: They bought a white goat for Eid.

questions.text: Why was Sara sad in 'Let's Be Helpful'?
options: Her father lost his job and could not buy her a new dress
questions.explanation: Sara's father lost his job and couldn't buy her a new dress for the fun fair.

questions.text: What event was the school going to arrange?
questions.explanation: The teacher announced the school would arrange a fun fair next month.

questions.text: Who suggested saving pocket money to buy Sara a dress?
questions.explanation: Maheen said, 'We will save our pocket money and buy Sara a new dress.'

questions.text: How did Sara feel when she opened the gift?
questions.explanation: She was surprised and her eyes filled with delight on seeing a new dress.

questions.text: What is the message of 'Let's Be Helpful'?
options: Do not go to fun fairs
questions.explanation: The lesson says sharing brings happiness; we should take care of each other.

questions.text: A dictionary lists words in:
questions.explanation: A dictionary lists words in alphabetical order with meanings and syllables.

questions.text: What is the national animal of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan.

questions.text: Markhor belongs to which animal family?
questions.explanation: It belongs to the goat family.

questions.text: Markhor is considered a symbol of:
questions.explanation: It is considered a symbol of bravery and intelligence.

questions.text: Markhor is known for its:
questions.explanation: It is known for its long and curly horns.

questions.text: How long are the horns of a male markhor, nearly?
questions.explanation: Horns on males are nearly 63 inches long; on females around 10 inches.

questions.text: Where is the markhor mostly found?
questions.explanation: It is mostly found in Northern Pakistan and the Himalayas.

questions.text: What is the average lifespan of a markhor?
questions.explanation: The average lifespan of a markhor is 10 to 13 years.

questions.text: Why were markhors killed by hunters in the past?
questions.explanation: They were hunted for their meat and horns, used in traditional medicine and as trophies.

questions.text: The contraction of 'will not' is:
questions.explanation: 'Will not' becomes 'won't'.

questions.text: What was Hafsa waiting for during the holidays?
questions.explanation: Hafsa anxiously waited for the storybooks her mother had ordered.

questions.text: Who brought the parcel to Hafsa's house?
questions.explanation: The postman handed her the parcel with a smile.

questions.text: What went wrong with the parcel?
options: The company sent the wrong books
questions.explanation: The book company had mistakenly sent some other books.

questions.text: What did Hafsa's mother decide to do?
options: Write a complaint to the seller
questions.explanation: She wrote a complaint letter to the seller so they could get the right parcel.

questions.text: What was the subject of the complaint letter?
questions.explanation: The letter's subject was 'Wrong Parcel'.

questions.text: The way a person's voice rises and falls while speaking is called:
questions.explanation: Intonation pattern is the way the voice rises and falls depending on what is said.

questions.text: What is the title of the poem in Unit 14 (Together We Live)?
questions.explanation: The poem in Unit 14 is 'Two Little Kittens'.

questions.text: When did the two little kittens begin to quarrel?
questions.explanation: 'Two little kittens, one stormy night, began to quarrel, and then to fight.'

questions.text: What did the old woman use to sweep the kittens out?
questions.explanation: 'The old woman took the sweeping broom and swept them both right out of the room.'

questions.text: How were the kittens when they crept back in?
options: Wet with snow and cold as ice
questions.explanation: They crept in 'all wet with snow and as cold as ice'.

questions.text: The kittens found it better to lie by the fire than to:
questions.explanation: They found it much better to lie by the fire than to quarrel and fight.

questions.text: What is the main idea of 'Two Little Kittens'?
options: Fighting brings trouble; living together peacefully is better
questions.explanation: The poem shows that quarrelling brings trouble, and living peacefully together is better.

questions.text: The regular repeated pattern of sounds in a poem is called:
questions.explanation: Rhythm is the regular repeated pattern of sounds.
